subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Aurora Finance
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: James O'Connor <j.oconnor@aurorafinance.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Aurora Finance

Hi James / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great kickoff. Below is a short recap of what we heard, success criteria, and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points
- Inconsistent latency during end-of-day batch processing and monthly statement generation (spikes from 150ms p95 to >800ms).
- Data isolation & compliance requirement for PII handling (Aurora needs dedicated tenancy for regulated workloads).
- High variance in TPS across day vs. peak monthly runs — you need predictable throughput for budgeting and procurement.

Current stack
- Inference: currently using public LLM API for chat summarization & entity extraction (mix of hosted endpoints).
- Orchestration: AWS Fargate + Step Functions for batch pipelines; some on-prem ETL for sensitive sources.
- Auth & keys: KMS in AWS for encryption; plans to onboard HSM for production.

Success criteria for Dedicated capacity fit
- Predictable throughput: baseline 250 TPS sustained with burst to 1,200 TPS for 10–15 minute windows.
- Latency: target generation p95 < 200ms for interactive flows; batch windows completed within existing SLA windows.
- Isolation: dedicated GPU pool, VPC peering, and customer-controlled KMS for keys.
- Cost transparency: fixed monthly committed capacity with clear overage/burst pricing.

Requirements & constraints called out in the call
- Model family: currently evaluating open-decoder models ~30B parameters; need guidance on quantization and expected perf.
- Autoscaling: want predictable autoscale policy with warm standby nodes for rapid burst.
- Observability: token-level billing and per-route latency breakdowns are required for your finance and ops teams.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Technical sizing call with Rafael to validate model/sequence-length assumptions and finalize GPU sizing (Rafael to propose times).
2) Sharing initial Dedicated estimate + mutual action plan (I attached an initial estimate and MAP for review).
3) Procurement checklist: once sizing is agreed, we’ll produce a SOW and dedicated contract with SLAs and SOC2 addendum.
4) Pilot: 4–6 week reserved pool pilot with telemetry and quality checks; criteria: throughput, p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens.

Attachments: aurora-dedicated-estimate.pdf, aurora-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks — if this looks right I’ll schedule Rafael’s deep-dive forWednesday/Thursday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
From: James O'Connor <j.oconnor@aurorafinance.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@aurorafinance.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Aurora Finance

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. This looks correct from our side. A few clarifications:

- TPS numbers: baseline of 250 TPS is right, but the peak burst can occasionally hit ~1,800 TPS for short windows (not just 1,200). We'll supply historical traffic patterns for the last 6 months.
- Models: we have a mix of smaller LLMs in production (~7B) and 30B for new product features; want to understand cost/latency tradeoffs between 30B quantized vs. 7B full precision.
- Security: SOC2 is essential. We will need an architecture diagram showing VPC peering and KMS flow to share with InfoSec.

Can Rafael propose times for a technical deep-dive tomorrow afternoon (PDT)? Priya and I are available after 2pm.

Thanks,
James
VP Product, Aurora Finance
j.oconnor@aurorafinance.com | +1 (646) 555-0123
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: James O'Connor <j.oconnor@aurorafinance.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Aurora Finance

Thanks James — appreciate the extra detail. A couple of technical notes / questions ahead of the deep-dive so we can come prepared:

1) Traffic profile: could you share a per-hour histogram for a representative week and one example of the monthly peak day? That will help size warm standby nodes vs. permanent baseline.
2) Sequence lengths: for the 30B use cases, what is the typical input + generation length (tokens)? Rough numbers (avg / 95th) are fine.
3) Data residency: for PII workloads, do you require on-prem hosting or is a VPC + customer-managed KMS in our cloud region acceptable?
4) Acceptance criteria for pilot: can you confirm success thresholds for throughput and latency and one business KPI (e.g., reduced end-of-day processing window from X hours to Y hours)?

I'll schedule a 60-minute deep-dive for Wed Jun 24 at 2:30pm PDT (invite to follow) — if that conflicts, let me know and I'll move. For the call I'll bring our infra lead and a runtime engineer to walk through kernel selection and autoscaling policies.

Rafael Mendes
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: James O'Connor <j.oconnor@aurorafinance.com>, Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@aurorafinance.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for Aurora Finance

James / Priya — great, thanks for the fast responses and for confirming availability. Quick update and next steps: 

- Rafael has scheduled the technical deep-dive for Wed Jun 24 at 2:30pm PDT (calendar invite sent). Rafael will cover sizing, autoscaling behavior, and quantization tradeoffs.
- Action items for Aurora: please send the traffic histograms and one example of your monthly peak day, plus token-length estimates for the 30B workloads before EOD Tuesday so Rafael can run initial sizing.
- From Redwood: we shared an initial estimate and mutual action plan (attached). After the deep-dive we'll produce a formal SOW and pilot plan.

If you want us to include legal/procurement early, Vanessa can loop in our contracts lead to start the SOW/PO template review.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
